commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendragurusarvabhouma, that dexterous saint who was like a bee at the lotus feet of Lord Sripathi Narayana, and a moon for the ocean of the philosophy of Sri Madhwacharya, delivered discourses on many literary works starting from "Pramanapaddhathi" of Sri Jayatheertha to "Tataparyachandrika" of Sri Vyasaraja in his sojourn at Srirangam.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रीशपादसरसीरुहभृङ्गः मध्वमौनिमतसिन्धुमृगाङ्कः मानपद्धतिमुखम् मतम् आख्यात् चन्द्रिकान्तम् असकृत् चतुरः असौ
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: श्रीशपादसरसीरुहभृङ्गः मध्वमौनिमतसिन्धुमृगाङ्कः चतुरः असौ मानपद्धतिमुखं चन्द्रिकान्तं मतम् असकृत् आख्यात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Like a honeybee at the lotus feet of Lord Vishnu and the moon delighting the ocean of sage Madhvacharya's philosophy, the skillful saint Raghavendra repeatedly and thoroughly expounded the doctrine through seminal texts ranging from Pramanapaddhati to Tatparyachandrika.

2.sa: प्राप्य रङ्गपरिणेतुरनुज्ञां तन्नियुक्तसकलर्तुसहायः । तत्कृपाकवचमात्मनि कुर्वन्नुत्तरां दिशमगाद्दुरुतेजाः ॥ २ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: After staying at Srirangam for some days, Sri Raghavendra of extraordinary resplendence left that place with Lord Sri Ranganatha's permission. With the blessings of Lord acting as the armour of protection for him, he found all the six Ruthus favourable to him and faced no inconvenience from the change of seasons. Leaving Srirangam, he set off towards north.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: प्राप्य रङ्गपरिणेतुः अनुज्ञाम् तत्-नियुक्त-सकल-ऋतु-सहायः तत्-कृपा-कवचम् आत्मनि कुर्वन् उत्तराम् दिशम् अगात् उरुतेजाः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: उरुतेजाः रङ्गपरिणेतुः अनुज्ञां प्राप्य तन्नियुक्तसकलर्तुसहायः तत्कृपाकवचम् आत्मनि कुर्वन् उत्तरां दिशम् अगात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having obtained the consent of Lord Ranganatha, Sri Raghavendra, endowed with immense radiance, donned the Lord's grace as his protective armor and, accompanied favorably by all the seasons directed by Him, set out toward the north.

3.sa: नामपर्वतमुपेत्य नृसिंहं नामसंस्मृतिधुताघजनौघम् । तं प्रणम्य तरुणार्यसमामं तां निशामिह गुरुर्वसति स्म ॥ ३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendratheertha reached the shrine of Lord Sri Narasimha at Namagiri. There he had the darshan of Lord Sri Narasimha whose radiance resembled that of the raising sun. Then he paid his obeisance in profound devotion to the Lord, the destroyer of sins of those who just chant his name, and spent that night there only.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: नामपर्वतम् उपेत्य नृसिंहम् नाम-संस्मृति-धुत-अघ-जन-ओघम् तम् प्रणम्य तरुणार्यसमामम् ताम् निशाम् इह गुरुः वसति स्म
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: गुरुः नामपर्वतम् उपेत्य नाम-संस्मृति-धुत-अघ-जन-ओघम् तरुणार्यसमामम् तम् नृसिंहम् प्रणम्य इह ताम् निशाम् वसति स्म
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having reached Namagiri (Namaparvata), Guru Sri Raghavendra bowed to Lord Narasimha, who destroys the sins of devotees merely remembering His name and shines like the morning sun, and stayed the night there.

4.sa: सोथ भल्लपुरि भैरवभट्टो वीरभद्र इति विश्रुतविद्वान् । नर्मणैव परिभूय नरेन्द्राद्धामरत्नमचिरात्समगृह्णात् ॥ ४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When Sri Raghavendra reached a place called Bhallapuri (Banavara), he was invited by two great scholars Bhairavabhatta and Veerabhadra for a debate. He defeated them effortlessly and was felicitated with the gift of a prosperous village by the master of that place.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: सः अथ भल्लपुरि भैरवभट्टः वीरभद्रः इति विश्रुतविद्वान् नर्मणा एव परिभूय नरेन्द्रात् धामरत्नम् अचिरात् समगृह्णात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अथ सः भल्लपुरि भैरवभट्टः वीरभद्रः इति विश्रुतविद्वान् नर्मणा एव परिभूय नरेन्द्रात् अचिरात् धामरत्नम् समगृह्णात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Upon arriving in Bhallapuri, Sri Raghavendra effortlessly defeated the renowned scholars Bhairavabhatta and Virabhadra in debate and promptly received a splendid village as an offering from the local king.

5.sa: विष्णुमङ्गलपुरे विलसन्तं देवमीक्ष्य विपुलश्रियभस्मात् । संवृतः परिजनैः स कुमारक्षेत्रमेत्य नमति स्म कुमारम् ॥ ५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra then came to Vishnumangala, where he had the darshan of the splendidly lustrous Lord Sri Mahavishnu. Leaving from there with his entourage, be reached Subramanyakshethra and paid his obeisance to Sri Subramanya there.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: विष्णुमङ्गलपुरे विलसन्तम् देवम् ईक्ष्य विपुलश्रियम् अस्मात् संवृतः परिजनैः सः कुमारक्षेत्रम् एत्य नमति स्म कुमारम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सः परिजनैः संवृतः विष्णुमङ्गलपुरे विलसन्तम् विपुलश्रियम् देवम् ईक्ष्य अस्मात् कुमारक्षेत्रम् एत्य कुमारम् नमति स्म
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having had darshana of the gloriously radiant Lord residing in Vishnumangalapura, Sri Raghavendra departed from there with his followers, reached Kumarakshetra, and bowed in devotion to Lord Kumara.

6.sa: श्वित्रिणोपि यदुपेत्य विमुक्तास्सद्य एव निजपातकसंघात् । सर्वसंपदभिवृद्धिकरोस्मिन्वासरान् कतिपयान्वसति स्म ॥ ६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Subramanyakshethra is a most divine place. Even lepers get completely cured from their disease if they circumbulate and pay their obeisance to Sri Subramanya there. Sri Raghavendra who bestows prosperity and success on those who are devoted to him stayed in a place of such divinity for some days.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्वित्रिणः अपि यत् उपेत्य विमुक्ताः सद्यः एव निज-पातक-संघात् सर्व-सम्पद्-अभिवृद्धि-करः अस्मिन् वासरान् कतिपयान् वसति स्म
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यत् उपेत्य श्वित्रिणः अपि सद्यः एव निज-पातक-संघात् विमुक्ताः (भवन्ति) सर्व-सम्पद्-अभिवृद्धि-करः (सः) अस्मिन् कतिपयान् वासरान् वसति स्म
commentaries.gemini_summary: Sri Raghavendra, who fosters all prosperity, stayed for several days in that sacred place (Subrahmanya Kshetra), where even lepers are immediately freed from all their sins upon arrival.

7.sa: रौप्यपीठपुरगं रुचिराङ्गं रुक्मिणीपतिमपश्यदुदारात् । पूर्णबोधगुरुभिः सकलज्ञैः सन्निधापितमघौघविदूरम् ॥ ७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The visual personality of Lord Balakrishna from head to toe is most beautiful. Each and every bit of his divine embodiment appears feastful to the eyes. He is the embodiment of infinite qualities and free from defects. Sri Madhawacharya has installed the idol of Lord Sri Krishna of such divinity at Udupi. Sri Raghavendra who reached Udupi had the darshan of Lord Sri Krishna, the consort of Rukmini there.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: रौप्यपीठपुरगम् रुचिराङ्गम् रुक्मिणीपतिम् अपश्यत् उदारात् पूर्णबोधगुरुभिः सकलज्ञैः सन्निधापितम् अघौघविदूरम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सकलज्ञैः पूर्णबोधगुरुभिः सन्निधापितम् अघौघविदूरं रौप्यपीठपुरगं रुचिराङ्गं रुक्मिणीपतिम् उदारात् अपश्यत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Sri Raghavendra beheld the exquisitely charming Lord Krishna (the consort of Rukmini) in the holy town of Raupyapitha (Udupi), who had been duly consecrated by the all-knowing preceptor Sri Madhvacharya and who dispels all sins.

8.sa: चन्द्रिकाविवरणं समतानीत्संचरन्नपि स पुण्यमहीषु । वेत्ति वर्णनिचयं समयानां संख्यया सह धियैष सहार्थैः ॥ ८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The most knowledgeable Sri Raghavendra was well versed with details of all the books such as the number of letters in each book and the meanings in concordance with the views contained in those books dealing with not only the philosophy of Sri Madhwacharya but also with other doctrines. In spite of his busy travel schedule, Sri Raghavendra wrote "Chandrika Prakasha" a commentary on that literary gem "Chandrika" of Sri Vyasaraja.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: चन्द्रिकाविवरणम् समतानीत् संचरन् अपि सः पुण्यमहीषु वेत्ति वर्णनिचयम् समयानाम् संख्यया सह धिया एषः सह अर्थैः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सः पुण्यमहीषु संचरन् अपि चन्द्रिकाविवरणम् समतानीत् । एषः धिया समयानाम् वर्णनिचयम् संख्यया सह अर्थैः सह वेत्ति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Even while travelling continuously through sacred lands, Sri Raghavendra composed his commentary on the Nyayamrita-Chandrika. Endowed with extraordinary intellect, he masterfully understood diverse philosophical doctrines along with their exact letter-counts and full meanings.

9.sa: चन्द्रिकाप्रवचनं दशकृत्वः सोकृतातिशयमात्मनि वाञ्छन् । पूर्णमास इव कर्मणि भूयोभ्यासमभ्यधिकतत्फलकाङ्क्षीः ॥ ९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: One who wishes to earn the benefit of the Poomamasa yaga in plenty conducts that Yaga repeatedly. Likewise Sri Raghavendra who was very sincere in his pursuit of more and more virtuousness in his task of writing commentary on "Chandrika" delivered scholarly discourse on that literary gem ten times.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: चन्द्रिका-प्रवचनम् दशकृत्वः सः अकृत अतिशयम् आत्मनि वाञ्छन् पूर्णमासे इव कर्मणि भूयः अभ्यासम् अभ्यधिक-तत्-फल-काङ्क्षी
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अभ्यधिक-तत्-फल-काङ्क्षी पूर्णमासे कर्मणि भूयः अभ्यासम् इव, आत्मनि अतिशयम् वाञ्छन् सः दशकृत्वः चन्द्रिका-प्रवचनम् अकृत ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Just as a person desiring greater spiritual rewards repeatedly performs the Purnamasa sacrifice, Sri Raghavendra, seeking internal excellence, delivered discourses on the Candrika ten times.

10.sa: सूत्रपात्ररुचिरं कलितर्धि न्यायपूर्वकसुधाज्यभरेण । तन्त्रदीपमनुबोधयदर्थं भाष्यवार्तिकमयं तनुते स्म ॥ १० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra wrote "Tantradeepika" which clearly interprets the meaning of all the Soothras being equipped with the wick of "Brahma Soothra Bhashya" which glows more and more brightly with the aid of the constantly flowing ghee of "Sri Nyayasudha" in that exquisite lamp of "Brahma Soothras".
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: सूत्र-पात्र-रुचिरम् कलित-ऋद्धिम् न्याय-पूर्वक-सुधा-आज्य-भरेण तन्त्र-दीपम् अनुबोधयद्-अर्थम् भाष्य-वार्तिक-मयम् तनुते स्म
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सूत्रपात्ररुचिरं न्यायपूर्वकसुधाज्यभरेण कलितर्द्धिं भाष्यवार्तिकमयं तन्त्रदीपम् अनुबोधयदर्थं [सः] तनुते स्म ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Sri Raghavendra composed the work 'Tantradipika' to illuminate the meaning of the Brahma Sutras. Conceived as a radiant lamp, it used the Sutras as its vessel, the rich commentary 'Nyayasudha' as ghee to feed its flame, and the insights of the Bhashya and Vartika as its very essence.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra also wrote "Nyayamoukthikamala" composed on the gold wire of "Brahmasootras" which adorned all the scholars as their necklace and which shone more and more when rubbed against the touch stone of the intellect of the great saint.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: ब्रह्मसूत्र-गण-काञ्चन-सूत्राम् कण्ठ-भूषणम् अशेष-बुधानाम् बुद्धि-शाण-परिशाण-विदीप्ताम् न्याय-मौक्तिक-ततीम् अतनिष्ट
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अशेष-बुधानाम् कण्ठ-भूषणम् ब्रह्मसूत्र-गण-काञ्चन-सूत्राम् बुद्धि-शाण-परिशाण-विदीप्ताम् न्याय-मौक्तिक-ततीम् अतनिष्ट ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: He (Sri Raghavendra) composed the work Nyayamauktikamala, a string of pearls of logic strung on the golden thread of the Brahma Sutras and polished brightly on the whetstone of his intellect, serving as an ornament for the neck of all scholars.

12.sa: चन्द्रिकाविवरणं न समाप्तं यावदेतदुभयं विरचय्य । न्यायगर्भनयवन्नयशाली तत्समापयदनन्तरमार्यः ॥ १२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra had profound knowledge about the ethics of shastras. He had started writing "Chandrikaprakasha" a commentary dealing exhausitively with description of the views of Sri Vyasaraja in his great literary masterpiece "Tatparyachandrika". Simultaneously he wrote two books "Tantradeepika" and "Nyayamoukthikamala". Then he completed writing "Chandrika Prakasha" which contained quotes from Poorvapaksha and Siddhantha strictly in conformity with the ethics of Shastras.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: चन्द्रिकाविवरणम् न समाप्तम् यावत् एतत् उभयम् विरचय्य न्यायगर्भनयवत् नयशाली तत् समापयत् अनन्तरम् आर्यः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: नयशाली आर्यः यावत् चन्द्रिकाविवरणम् न समाप्तम् (तावत्) एतत् उभयम् विरचय्य अनन्तरम् न्यायगर्भनयवत् तत् समापयत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: While his commentary on the Chandrika was still incomplete, the wise and noble Raghavendra composed the two preceding works, and subsequently completed the commentary endowed with profound logical maxims.

13.sa: भाव्यसंशयमहो गुरुवंशे दर्शनश्रुतिपरस्सुमतीन्द्रः । तस्य सार्थकमिदं सकलं स्यादित्यवेत्य कृतवान् कृतिसार्थम् ॥ १३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra contributed great literary works to the philosophical world of Sri Madhwacharya, as he knew that those books would be surely helpful to one who would be adorning the throne of learning of Mahasamsthana in future by name Sri Sumatheendratheertha who would be a great scholar and who would be deeply interested in teaching and delivering discourses on those literary works. This is really amazing! Sri Appannacharya while extolling Sri Raghavendra in '"Gurustotra" has stated that the great saint had intuitive knowledge about the part and the future. The above fact exemplifies beyond doubt this statement of Sri Appannacharya.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: भावी असंंशयम् अहो गुरुवंशे दर्शन-श्रुति-परः सुमतीन्द्रः तस्य सार्थकम् इदम् सकलम् स्यात् इति अवेत्य कृतवान् कृति-सार्थम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अहो गुरुवंशे दर्शन-श्रुति-परः सुमतीन्द्रः असंंशयं भावी, तस्य इदं सकलं सार्थकं स्यात् इति अवेत्य (श्रीराघवेंद्रः) कृति-सार्थं कृतवान्।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Foreseeing that the deeply scholarly Sumatīndra would undoubtedly appear in the guru lineage devoted to philosophical learning and exposition, Śrī Rāghavendra composed a magnificent collection of literary works so that they would find their full and fruitful purpose through him.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra very well knew what to do and when to do. He had many disciples. Everybody was delighted when those disiples celebrated all the festivities connected with all the six Ruthus under the able guidance of their guru Sri Raghavendra.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: राघवेन्द्र-यतिराट् असमानैः उत्सवैः बहु-विधैः उचित-ज्ञः कारितैः ऋतुषु षट्सु अपि शिष्यैः लोक-मण्डलम् अमन्दयत् एषः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: उचित-ज्ञः एषः राघवेन्द्र-यतिराट् षट्सु अपि ऋतुषु शिष्यैः कारितैः असमानैः बहु-विधैः उत्सवैः लोक-मण्डलम् अमन्दयत्।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Knowing what was fitting for each occasion, Sri Raghavendra delighted the world through the diverse and peerless festivals celebrated by his disciples across all six seasons.

15.sa: श्रीरामदेवस्य महोत्सवे हरिं विलोक्य तं सेवितुमादरादिव । मनोज्ञमाकन्दमरन्दधारया कृताभिषेकः सुरभिः समाययौ ॥ १५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Those who come to the temples take bath before going there to offer their worship to the God. Likewise, when the auspicious day of Sri Rama Navami approached, Vasantha Ruthu (the Spring) set in after bathing in the nectar of the just blooming mango flowers and the cool breeze spreading the sweet fragrance of that nectar everywhere as if to worship Sri Moolaramachandra.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रीरामदेवस्य महोत्सवे हरिम् विलोक्य तम् सेवितुम् आदरात् इव मनोज्ञ-माकन्द-मरन्द-धारया कृत-अभिषेकः सुरभिः समाययौ
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: श्रीरामदेवस्य महोत्सवे तम् हरिम् विलोक्य आदरात् सेवितुम् इव मनोज्ञ-माकन्द-मरन्द-धारया कृत-अभिषेकः सुरभिः समाययौ ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Seeing Lord Hari during the grand festival of Sri Rama, the Spring season (Surabhi) arrived, having bathed in the sweet stream of mango nectar, as if eager to serve the Lord with deep reverence.

16.sa: मधुस्तदा मन्मथसार्वभौमे विनिर्गते मानभृतां जयाय । प्रसूनमाध्वीकणसेकतोसावरण्यवीथीरकरोदपांसूः ॥ १६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When a king sets out of his palace, his subjects sweep the ground all along his route and sprinkle water so that it is free from the rising dust. Similarly, when the emperor Manmatha set out to pacify those girls who were amorously indignant and to inspire them to unite with their lovers, his servant Vasantha sprinkled nectar of flowers all along his route in the forest and cleaned it so that it became free from dust.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मधुः तदा मन्मथ-सार्वभौमे विनिर्गते मानभृताम् जयाय प्रसून-माध्वी-कण-सेकतः असौ अरण्य-वीथीः अकरोत् अपांसूः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तदा मन्मथ-सार्वभौमे मानभृताम् जयाय विनिर्गते असौ मधुः प्रसून-माध्वी-कण-सेकतः अरण्य-वीथीः अपांसूः अकरोत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: When the emperor of love (Manmatha) set out to conquer proudly indignant lovers, spring (Madhu) cleared the forest pathways of dust by sprinkling drops of flower nectar.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When Manda marutha (the cool breeze) carrying the sweet fragrance emanating from the trees of sandalwood at the pinnacle of Malayapravatha was flowing gently it appeared as if he was walking on the sprouts of leaves of trees with those flowers as gentle smile on his face and creating a noise that sounded like the buzzing of bees.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: शनैः शनैः चन्दन-भूधरात् यान् मरुत्-कुमारः तरु-पल्लवेषु विन्यस्य पादम् कुसुमैः स-हासैः स-चङ्क्रमः अभूत् भ्रमर-प्रणादः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: चन्दनभूधरात् शनैः शनैः यान् भ्रमरप्रणादः मरुत्कुमारः सहासैः कुसुमैः तरुपल्लवेषु पादं विन्यस्य सचङ्क्रमः अभूत्।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Moving gently from the sandalwood-scented Malaya mountain, the youthful breeze strolled through the grove, stepping upon tender sprouts among smiling blossoms with the humming of bees resounding as his voice.

18.sa: वल्लरीषु मलयाचलानिलस्पन्दितासु परपुष्टभामिनी । कामदिग्विजयकाहलनादभ्रान्तिदं निगदमातनुते स्म ॥ १८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When the bunches of blooming flowers were swinging to and fro by the force of the fragrant breeze emanating from Malayaparvatha, the female cuckoo was singing "Kuhoo Kuhoo" in panchamaraga which created an illusion that it was the bugle sound of the victory of Manmatha.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वल्लरीषु मलयाचल-अनिल-स्पन्दितासु परपुष्ट-भामिनी काम-दिग्विजय-काहल-नाद-भ्रान्ति-दम् निगदम् आतनुते स्म
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मलयाचलानिलस्पन्दितासु वल्लरीषु परपुष्टभामिनी कामदिग्विजयकाहलनादभ्रान्तिदं निगदम् आतनुते स्म।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Upon the creepers gently stirred by the southern breeze from the Malaya mountain, the female cuckoo sang a sweet call that sounded like the trumpet-blast heralding the world-conquest of Kama, the god of love.

19.sa: मल्लिकासुमसमुत्थरजोभिर्वल्लिकाभिरभितः कृतभूषः । मारनीरशरधिर्मधुमासः प्रादुरास पथिकासु दुरासः ॥ १९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The month of Chaitra which was decorated with creepers covered with farina of Jasmine flowers; which afflicted those who being apart from their sweethearts were journeying; and which was like the quiver of Manmatha started then.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मल्लिकासुमसमुत्थरजोभिः वल्लिकाभिः अभितः कृतभूषः मारनीरशरधिः मधुमासः पथिकासु दुरासः प्रादुरास
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मल्लिकासुमसमुत्थरजोभिः वल्लिकाभिः अभितः कृतभूषः मारनीरशरधिः पथिकासु दुरासः मधुमासः प्रादुरास
commentaries.gemini_summary: The spring month of Chaitra arrived, adorned on all sides by creepers laden with the pollen of jasmine blossoms, acting like a quiver of arrows for Kama and becoming utterly unbearable to travelers separated from their beloveds.

20.sa: आगतो जनिमघुर्मधुरश्रीर्मानमत्र ननु मन्दसमीरः । हन्त पान्थजन न त्यज कान्तामित्यघुष्यदधिकं कलकण्ठः ॥ २० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "Vasantha who is splendidly shining with radiance has already arrived. The mild breeze filled with sweet fragrance testifies this fact. This is really true. Oh poor travellers! do not stay away from your sweethearts". This was how the cuckoo shouted then.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: आगतः जनिम् मधुः मधुरश्रीः मानम् अत्र ननु मन्दसमीरः हन्त पान्थजन न त्यज कान्ताम् इति अघुष्यत् अधिकम् कलकण्ठः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मधुरश्रीः मधुः जनिम् आगतः अत्र मन्दसमीरः ननु मानम् हन्त पान्थजन कान्तां न त्यज इति कलकण्ठः अधिकम् अघुष्यत्
commentaries.gemini_summary: The cuckoo loudly proclaimed that the charming spring season had arrived—as testified by the gentle breeze—and exhorted travellers not to leave their beloveds.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sprouts of leaves had sprung up in the branches of trees in Vasantha Ruthu. They were sparkling like flash and were waving by the force of the wind. Nectar was flowing like rainfall from the blooming flowers in those trees which were like clouds. Thus the days of the spring were looking like the days of the monsoon accompanied by lightning and heavy showers.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: चञ्चलद्युतिसमद्युतिचञ्चत्पल्लवावलिपरीतजनेषु स्यन्दमानमधुवर्षिषु कामम् वर्षवासरम् अहानि अनुचक्रुः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: चञ्चलद्युतिसमद्युतिचञ्चत्पल्लवावलिपरीतजनेषु स्यन्दमानमधुवर्षिषु (वसन्ते) अहानि कामं वर्षवासरम् अनुचक्रुः ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Surrounded by trembling rows of tender sprouts that glittered like lightning and showered flowing nectar, the days of spring closely resembled the days of the rainy season.

22.sa: मारुताभिमुखषट्पदमण्डल्याकृतिस्मृतिभवापथिकेषु । अन्तकं मुधतया दिदीशे किं कुण्डलीकृतिरहो कुटिलेन ॥ २२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Bees were moving in a circle against the wind in Vasantha Ruthu. The group of those bees in the shape of a coil looked like a swarthy snake assigned by Manmatha with the task of killing those men who had stayed away from their sweethearts. As Manmatha does not kill gradually like Yama does, he had made Yama worthless with regard to the killing of those travellers.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मारुत-अभिमुख-षट्पद-मण्डली-आकृतिः स्मृतिभवा पथिकेषु अन्तकम् मुधतया दिदीशे किम् कुण्डली-कृतिः अहो कुटिलेन
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अहो कुटिलेन स्मृतिभवा मारुत-अभिमुख-षट्पद-मण्डली-आकृतिः कुण्डली-कृतिः पथिकेषु अन्तकम् मुधतया दिदीशे किम् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet imagines that the coiled, snake-like swarm of bees flying against the wind was dispatched by the crooked Kāmadeva to torment travellers separated from their beloveds, rendering Yama (Death) completely redundant.

23.sa: पुष्पपल्लवमुखेन महान्तं पर्युपास्त समयः पुरुषं यत् । माधवश्रियमगान्महनीयामप्रियामयमयोगिजनस्य ॥ २३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Vasantha worshipped the great saint Sri Raghavendra with flowers and shoots of leaves. As a result of this he gained plenty of wealth (lustre). This wealth of Vasantha was not congenial to those saintly men who stayed away from their sweethearts.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पुष्प-पल्लव-मुखेन महान्तम् पर्युपास्त समयः पुरुषम् यत् माधव-श्रियम् अगात् महनीयाम् अप्रियाम् अयम् अयोगि-जनस्य
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: समयः पुष्पपल्लवमुखेन महान्तं पुरुषं यत् पर्युपास्त (तेन) अयम् अयोगिजनस्य अप्रियाम् महनीयां माधवश्रियम् अगात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Because the spring season worshipped the great saint with flowers and tender sprouts, it attained the glorious splendor of spring (or of Lord Madhava), which caused distress to lovers separated from their partners.

24.sa: शाखिनः किसललोहितमौलिप्रावृतिं विरचयन्नृतुपुंसः । बाणमेव मदनोक्कृतबर्हिर्दृष्टमध्वगवधाय वनेषु ॥ २४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: It is suitable to conduct Abhicharayaga for the purpose of killing the enemy. One who is engaged in yaga should wear a red turbon. Weapons like sword, etc. should be strewn around the pot of consecrated fire in place of Kusa Grass. Now Vasantha has initiated himself to conduct yaga for the purpose of killing (to cause affliction whose effect was as agonising as that of death to) those who had stayed away from their sweethearts. The trees have provided red turban and Manmatha has provided weapons like arrows of flowers to be strewn around the fire pot for Vasantha. The Vasantha Ruthu was stimulating for those who were bereft of their lovers.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: शाखिनः किसल-लोहित-मौलि-प्रावृतिम् विरचयन् ऋतु-पुंसः बाणम् एव मदन-उत्कृत-बर्हिः दृष्टम् अध्वग-वधाय वनेषु
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: वनेषु अध्वग-वधाय ऋतु-पुंसः किसल-लोहित-मौलि-प्रावृतिम् विरचयन् शाखिनः मदन-उत्कृत-बर्हिः बाणम् एव दृष्टम्
commentaries.gemini_summary: Spring is poetically imagined as performing a destructive rite (abhicāra) in the forest to afflict separated travelers. The trees provide him with a red turban of tender sprouts, and Cupid arranges his floral arrows as the sacrificial grass.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Beautiful girls whose attractive bosoms looked like golden pots, in their acts of amusement kicked one of the Ashoka trees. The tree was delighted by those rare kicks so much so that bunches of flowers appeared immediately on its branches. Buds of beautiful flowers started splendidly shining on the branches of that tree. If appears as if that Ashoka tree was thrilled by the kicks of those beautiful girls.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: शातकुम्भमय-कुम्भ-कुचानाम् अङ्घ्रिपातम् अतिदुर्लभम् एत्य संमदेन सहसा किम् अशोकः कुड्मलैः अभवत् अथ पुलकाङ्गः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अथ शातकुम्भमयकुम्भकुचानाम् अतिदुर्लभम् अङ्घ्रिपातम् एत्य संमदेन अशोकः सहसा कुड्मलैः पुलकाङ्गः अभवत् किम् ?
commentaries.gemini_summary: Upon receiving the rare touch of the feet of maidens with golden-pitcher-like breasts, the Ashoka tree was filled with immense joy, blossoming with buds that seemed like horripilations of delight on its body.

26.sa: स्त्रीकृतं विदधिरे सुमनोभिः स्वाङ्गिसेवनमशोकमनङ्गम् । धार्मिकं च सुदृशः सततं तौ हन्त पान्थजनहन्तृपदे स्तः ॥ २६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Those beautiful girls with attractive eyes kicked the Ashoka tree with their feet. The Ashoka tree which felt as though its wish was fulfilled by accepting those Kicks gleefully, shone with flowers. Then those girls worshipped with Ashoka flowers, the feet of Manmatha who led a righteous life (in the bow of flowers). Thus both the Ashoka tree and Manmatha caused grief to those who were bereft of their lovers. The effect of that grief was as agonising as that of death.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: स्त्रीकृतम् विदधिरे सुमनोभिः स्वाङ्गिसेवनम् अशोकम् अनङ्गम् धार्मिकम् च सुदृशः सततम् तौ हन्त पान्थजनहन्तृपदे स्तः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सुदृशः सुमनोभिः अशोकम् अनङ्गम् च स्त्रीकृतम् स्वाङ्गिसेवनम् विदधिरे । धार्मिकम् (अपि) तौ सततम् पान्थजनहन्तृपदे स्तः , हन्त !
commentaries.gemini_summary: The beautiful-eyed women honored the Ashoka tree and the god of love (Ananga) with flowers and the touch of their limbs; yet alas, despite being treated so religiously, both of them constantly act as tormentors and slayers of separated travelers.

27.sa: पुष्पितस्य बकुलस्य समन्तादुद्गतास्सुमनसः सुमनोभिः । अङ्गनास्य मधुनाध्वगयूनामापदागमनमत्र शशंसुः ॥ २७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Beautiful girls who were as soft as flowers sprinkled intoxicated drink from their mouths on bakula trees. Immediately flowers appeared on those trees. The birth of those flowers in the forest in Vasantha Ruthu alluded that peril was lurking over those who were away from their sweethearts.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पुष्पितस्य बकुलस्य समन्तात् उद्गताः सुमनसः सुमनोभिः अङ्गना-आस्य-मधुना अध्वग-यूनाम् आपद्-आगमनम् अत्र शशंसुः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अत्र सुमनोभिः अङ्गना-आस्य-मधुना पुष्पितस्य बकुलस्य समन्तात् उद्गताः सुमनसः अध्वग-यूनाम् आपद्-आगमनम् शशंसुः ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The flowers blooming all around the Bakula tree, made to blossom by the mouthfuls of wine sprayed by lovely women, announced the impending distress of separation for young travelers.

28.sa: रामचन्द्रमथ रामनवम्यामिष्टदैवममृतेरुपकॢप्तैः । पञ्चभिः परमराघवयोगी भक्तिपूर्वमभिषिञ्चति तत्र ॥ २८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The great saint Sri Raghavendra with profound devotion worshipped Lord Sri Moolarama, the God who fulfills one's wishes, with ablution of panchmrutha on the auspicious day of Sri Ramanavami in such an enchanting Vasantha Ruthu.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: रामचन्द्रम् अथ रामनवम्याम् इष्टदैवम् अमृतैः उपकॢप्तैः पञ्चभिः परमराघवयोगी भक्तिपूर्वम् अभिषिञ्चति तत्र
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अथ तत्र परमराघवयोगी रामनवम्याम् उपकॢप्तैः पञ्चभिः अमृतैः इष्टदैवं रामचन्द्रं भक्तिपूर्वम् अभिषिञ्चति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Then, on the sacred occasion of Sri Rama Navami, the supreme ascetic Sri Raghavendra Yogi performed the ceremonial ablution (abhisheka) of his cherished deity Lord Ramachandra with profound devotion using the prepared fivefold nectars (panchamrita).

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Greeshma Ruthu which nourishes the young girl "Mallika Latha" (the creeper of Jasmine) in her juvenility; which causes disrespect to Manmatha; which protects the forest conflagration; which dries up water in ponds and other reservoirs set in. Explanation: Jasmine flowers grow in plenty during summer. Since the lovers does not get aroused amorously during summer, Manmatha gets slighted as a result of his defeat. Conflagration appears in forests. Glare and heat of the sun dries up the water in reservoirs. The poet has described these factors in this stanza.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मल्लिका-युवति-यौवन-धाता मन्मथ-प्रभु-परीभव-दाता कानन-ज्वलन-बालक-माता वासरः अजनि सरः-जल-पाता
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मल्लिका-युवति-यौवन-धाता मन्मथ-प्रभु-परीभव-दाता कानन-ज्वलन-बालक-माता सरः-जल-पाता वासरः अजनि।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The summer day arrived, fostering the youthful bloom of the jasmine creeper, diminishing the power of Cupid, nourishing the infant forest fire, and drying up the waters of the lakes.

30.sa: जृम्भिते च मिहिरे भुवि शैत्यं कूपमाप तरुणीकुचदुर्गम् । किंचिदन्यदिनसंधिमवांशुं छायया सह परं चरति स्म ॥ ३० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: As the frigidity could not tolerate the scorching heat of the sun in Greeshma Ruthu, it hid in the water in wells and the bosoms of young girls. A small quantity of frigidity which had the intention of living and emerging stronger in the company of the remaining days of that Ruthu, befriended the shadow of the trees. Explanation: The poet has suggested in this stanza that water in the wells, the bosoms of young girls and the shadow of the trees appear very cool during Greshma Ruthu.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: जृम्भिते च मिहिरे भुवि शैत्यम् कूपम् आप तरुणी-कुच-दुर्गम् किञ्चित् अन्य-दिन-सन्धिम् अवांशुम् छायया सह परम् चरति स्म
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मिहिरे जृम्भिते (सति) च भुवि शैत्यम् कूपम् तरुणी-कुच-दुर्गम् आप किञ्चित् अन्य-दिन-सन्धिम् अवांशुम् छायया सह परं चरति स्म
commentaries.gemini_summary: When the sun blazed intensely across the earth, the coolness fled for shelter into deep wells and the fortress-like bosoms of young maidens, while a small fraction of it moved about only in the company of shade, waiting for milder days.

31.sa: तापयत्यतितरां तरणिर्यल्लोकबन्धुरिति नाम कथं स्यात् । तत्सखस्य शुचिता शुचिमासश्चटका भुवि विचुकुशुरित्थम् ॥ ३१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: "The sun causes lasstitude to the people with his glare and scorching heat. Then how could he be hailed as Lokabandhu (friend of this world) How could the month of Ashadha, the friend of the sun be attributed with purity? This was how the chataka birds (cuculus melanoleucus ...the bird said to live only on raindrops) were raving in Greeshma Ruthu.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: तापयति अतितराम् तरणिः यत् लोकबन्धुः इति नाम कथम् स्यात् तत्-सखस्य शुचिता शुचि-मासः चटकाः भुवि विचुकुशुः इत्थम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तरणिः यत् अतितराम् तापयति, [तस्य] 'लोकबन्धुः' इति नाम कथम् स्यात्? तत्-सखस्य शुचि-मासस्य शुचिता [च कथम् स्यात् इति] इत्थम् भुवि चटकाः विचुकुशुः।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The cātaka birds on earth lamented, asking how the sun could be named 'Lokabandhu' (friend of the world) when he scorches so excessively, and how his companion, the summer month (Śuci), could be attributed with purity (śucitā).

32.sa: छायया सह दिवैव कराग्रैः शम्बरम्बरहरेम्बररले । ज्येष्ठपूर्वमभियायिनि नूनं कोपताम्रनयना नलिनीति ॥ ३२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The sun shines in the sky like a gem. When he steals the cloth of water with his rays meaning when he dries up the water, it appears as though a virtuous man is disrobing the wife of another man. The sun steals the shadow and dries up the water with his scorching heat during the day time itself. He arrives putting the month of Jyesta down in his front. This creates an impression that the sun is doing all these things in collusion with jyestha (elder brother). When Padmini (group of lotus flowers), the sun's wellwisher witnessed all these, she turned red with great anger.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: छायया सह दिवा एव कर-अग्रैः शम्बर-अम्बर-हरे अम्बर-रत्ने ज्येष्ठ-पूर्वम् अभियायिनि नूनम् कोप-ताम्र-नयना नलिनी इति
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अम्बर-रत्ने दिवा एव कर-अग्रैः छायया सह शम्बर-अम्बर-हरे ज्येष्ठ-पूर्वम् अभियायिनि (सति) नलिनी नूनम् कोप-ताम्र-नयना (अभवत्) इति
commentaries.gemini_summary: As the sun, the jewel of the sky, used his scorching rays to steal away both shade and water (garment) during the day while advancing in the month of Jyeshtha, the lotus pond appeared to turn red-eyed in anger (blooming red with indignation at his audacity).

33.sa: भाविशोषणमवेत्य दुरन्तं पद्मसायकहिताय पयांसि । कामिनीकुचतटेषु वसन्तो विन्यधत्त यदिमावतिशीतौ ॥ ३३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Vasantha very well knew that the water gets dried up in Greeshma Ruthu. Therefore, with the interest of Manmatha in his mind, he filled all the water in the pot like bosoms of women. This is the reason why the bosoms of women feel very cool in Greeshma Ruthu.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: भाविशोषणम् अवेत्य दुरन्तम् पद्मसायकहिताय पयांसि कामिनीकुचतटेषु वसन्तः विन्यधत्त यत् इमौ अतिशीतौ
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: वसन्तः दुरन्तं भाविशोषणम् अवेत्य पद्मसायकहिताय पयांसि कामिनीकुचतटेषु विन्यधत्त यत् इमौ अतिशीतौ (स्तः)
commentaries.gemini_summary: Foreseeing the severe drying up of waters in the coming summer, Spring stored waters in the breasts of beautiful women for the sake of Cupid (Manmatha), which explains why their breasts remain extraordinarily cool.

34.sa: वारिनर्मपरियौवतवक्षोजातसङ्गमवशात्सरसीनाम् । शैत्यमाप परितप्तजडानां किं न यच्छति सुवृत्तसमाजः ॥ ३४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When those beautiful girls were sporting in water in groups, even the water in the ponds which had become hot by the scorching heat of the sun became cool as a result of its contact with the cool bosoms of those girls. A Society of virtous people helps even the sluggards who are facing hardship due to poverty. Likewise, the plumpy round bosoms of those girls with their embrace relieve those who are deprived of the companionship of their sweethearts from their agony of separation.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वारि-नर्म-परि-यौवत-वक्षोजात-सङ्गम-वशात् सरसीनाम् शैत्यम् आप परितप्त-जडानाम् किम् न यच्छति सुवृत्त-समाजः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: वारिनर्मपरियौवतवक्षोजातसङ्गमवशात् सरसीनाम् (वारि) शैत्यम् आप । सुवृत्तसमाजः परितप्तजडानाम् किं न यच्छति ?
commentaries.gemini_summary: Due to contact with the breasts of the young women playfully sporting in the water, the sun-heated water of the lakes became delightfully cool. Indeed, what benefit does the company of the virtuous (and round-breasted) not bestow upon the afflicted and dull (or heated water)?

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The night causes separation for the ruddy geese. Therefore they treat the moon, the king of night as their enemy. The moonlight causes panic in them like the abattoir of a butcher does. Thus those ruddy geese used to turn pale out of fear of the night, the moon and the moonlight. But when the summer began, days became longer and the nights became shorter. The poet has exaggerated that it appeared as if the pair of those ruddy geese presented a gift to the days of Greeshma Ruthu blessing thus, "let the days become longer and the nights shorter".
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वैरि-चन्द्र-गुण-प्रथण-भीत्या चक्रवाक-मिथुनम् परिशुष्यत् आतपत्र-विलसत्-बिससेभ्यः पारितोषिकम् अदात् परिणाहम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: वैरि-चन्द्र-गुण-प्रथण-भीत्या परिशुष्यत् चक्रवाक-मिथुनम् आतपत्र-विलसत्-बिससेभ्यः (दिवसेभ्यः) पारितोषिकम् परिणाहम् अदात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Distressed by the fear of the waxing moonlight of their enemy, the moon, the pair of ruddy geese (Chakravakas) presented length and expansion as a reward to the sunny summer days (thereby making the days longer).

36.sa: सामवर्तिहरितं ससुतेति प्राप्य तां हृतवसुर्दिशयार्कः । दूरतः परिहरन्नथ पश्चात्तापतः प्रतिययौ धनदाशाम् ॥ ३६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Thinking that his wife must be staying with his son Yama, the sun first went towards south. But when the south stole all his rays, he left south and went repenting towards north that belonged to Kubera. Explanation: A rich man learning that his wife is staying happily with his son, goes to her, thinking that being a good woman she talks very sweetly. But when his wife steals all his belongings, he repents and goes to a king or to another rich man who is very generous. The poet says that the sun has followed the same universal usage. The summary of this stanza is that the sun moves towards south in Dakshinayana (the winter solistice) and towards north in Uttarayana (the summer solistice)
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: सामवर्ति-हरितम् स-सुता इति प्राप्य ताम् हृत-वसुः दिशया अर्कः दूरतः परिहरन् अथ पश्चात्तापतः प्रतिययौ धनद-आशाम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अर्कः स-सुता इति तां सामवर्ति-हरितम् प्राप्य दिशया हृत-वसुः अथ पश्चात्तापतः दूरतः परिहरन् धनद-आशाम् प्रतिययौ ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Thinking that the southern quarter was with his son (Yama), the Sun approached it, but when stripped of his wealth/rays by that direction, he repented and retreated far away toward the northern quarter (the realm of Kubera).

37.sa: तत्र तत्रभवतायतिनेत्रा राघवेन्द्रगुरुणा क्रियते स्म । फुल्लतल्लजसरोजसरस्यां जानकीपरिवृढप्लवकेली ॥ ३७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The most venerable saint Sri Raghavendra organised Theppothsava (rowing an idol in a decorated boat) of Lord Sri Moolarama, the consort of Seethadevi in the lake full of blossomed lotus flowers through his disciples in Greeshma Ruthu.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: तत्र तत्रभवता यतिनेत्रा राघवेन्द्रगुरुणा क्रियते स्म फुल्लतल्लजसरोजसरस्याम् जानकीपरिवृढप्लवकेली
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तत्र यतिनेत्रा तत्रभवता राघवेन्द्रगुरुणा फुल्लतल्लजसरोजसरस्याम् जानकीपरिवृढप्लवकेली क्रियते स्म ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: In that place, the venerable Guru Raghavendra, leader among ascetics, organized and celebrated the boat-festival (teppotsava) of Lord Rama (the husband of Janaki) in a lake filled with splendid blooming lotuses.

38.sa: पूर्णरोचिषि तुषारमधीचौ भानुमालिनि गतेम्बरमध्यम् । योयमारभत कर्म हि चातुर्मास्यनाम रचयन् हरिपूर्जां ॥ ३८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Rows of dark clouds completely covered the sun. The swans left for Manasa sarovar. The peacock, the vehicle of Subramanya who is the son of Himavanta's daughter Parvathi, started dancing. Manmatha's friend Varsha Ruthu which stimulates those suffering from the pangs of separation from their lovers set in.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पूर्णरोचिषि तुषारामरीचौ भानुमालिनि गते अम्बरमध्यम् यः अयम् आरभत कर्म हि चातुर्मास्यनाम रचयन् हरिपूजाम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पूर्णरोचिषि भानुमालिनि अम्बरमध्यम् गते (सति), यः अयम् हरिपूजाम् रचयन् चातुर्मास्यनाम कर्म हि आरभत।
commentaries.gemini_summary: When the brilliantly shining sun reached the middle of the sky, Sri Raghavendra commenced the sacred observance known as Chaturmasya, performing dedicated worship to Lord Hari.

39.sa: तद्धृतेरनुदिनं क्रियमाणेष्वेकवासरकृतं विभवं यः । कश्चिदाह यदि हन्त निवृत्तिं ब्राह्मणः श्रुतिततिं स लभेत ॥ ३९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The bridegroom wears red sacrificial thread dipped in vermilion before marrying. Keeping this in mind, the poet has described the reddist rainbow. He says that the just rising rainbow looked like the sacrificial thread (the sky) of Lord Sri Narayana who is going to marry Lakshmi, the sister of the moon (monsoon). It has turrned reddish as it was dipped in vermilion. The sacrificial thread of Lord Sri Narayana looked beautiful. This is how the poet has described the rainbow which appears reddish in monsoon.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: तत्-धृतेः अनुदिनम् क्रियमाणेषु एक-वासर-कृतम् विभवम् यः कश्चित् आह यदि हन्त निवृत्तिम् ब्राह्मणः श्रुति-ततिम् सः लभेत
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यः कश्चित् ब्राह्मणः तत्-धृतेः अनुदिनम् क्रियमाणेषु एक-वासर-कृतम् विभवम् यदि आह, हन्त सः श्रुति-ततिम् निवृत्तिम् लभेत ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: If any Brahmana could fully describe the immense magnificence of what was performed in merely a single day among the daily royal benefactions, he might as well attain the exhaustive mastery of the entire body of the Vedas, indicating the impossible grandeur of the king's daily patronage.

40.sa: वारिदावलितिरोहितमित्रं मानसाभिमुखपाण्डुरपत्रम् । नृत्यदद्रितनयासुतपत्रं दीव्यति स्म दिनमब्जमित्रम् ॥ ४० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When the clouds absorb water in summer, they swallow heaps of red lotus along with water. During monsoon, those clouds shower water along with the lotus they have swallowed as rains. The red fire flies during that season look like those lotus flowers showering as rains. Those insects which are red like pieces of ruby and coral shine more splendidly than the ruby and the coral themselves. The poet has described that the earth gets completely covered by such insects during monsoon.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वारिदावलितिरोहितमित्रम् मानसाभिमुखपाण्डुरपत्रम् नृत्यत्-अद्रितनयासुतपत्रम् दीव्यति स्म दिनम् अब्जमित्रम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: वारिदावलितिरोहितमित्रम् मानसाभिमुखपाण्डुरपत्रम् नृत्यदद्रितनयासुतपत्रम् दिनम् अब्जमित्रम् दीव्यति स्म ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: During the rainy season, the day shone with the sun hidden behind lines of clouds, white swans flying towards Lake Manasa, and peacocks (the mount of Kartikeya) dancing with joy.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Girls comb their hair and part their forelock to form a line. Then they apply vermilion all along that line. The lightning was shining like sapphire amidst the rows of black clouds during monsoon. The poet has described that the lightning shone like the line of vermillion applied on the line parting the forelock of that beautiful girl (Monsoon).
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: प्रावृट् इन्दु-सहजाम् परिणेतुः शब्द-मण्डल-समाश्रय-शौरेः कुङ्कुमाक्तम् अचिरात् उपवीतम् पाकशासन-शरास-मिषात् आभात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: प्रावृट् इन्दुसहजाम् परिणेतुः शब्दमण्डलसमाश्रयशौरेः कुङ्कुमाक्तम् उपवीतं पाकशासनशरासमिषात् अचिरात् आभात्
commentaries.gemini_summary: During the rainy season, the rainbow shone in the sky as if it were a saffron-smeared sacred thread donned by Lord Vishnu, who dwells amidst the thunderous clouds, as He prepares to wed Lakshmi (the Moon's sister).

42.sa: पीतपुष्करकलापपयोभ्यो निर्गतैरिव जलैर्जलदेभ्यः । पद्मरागमणिविद्रुमभङ्गैरिन्द्रगोपनिकरैः स्थगिता भूः ॥ ४२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: It is proclaimed in the Puranas that the saint Agasthya who lived in Malayachala in the south dried up the swelling ocean by consuming the entire quantity of water. The poet while describing the act of clouds moving towards south during monsoon has said that it appeared as though those clouds were moving in the direction of south to learn from the saint the hymn in respect of drinking water from the sea.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पीतपुष्करकलापपयोभ्यः निर्गतैः इव जलैः जलदेभ्यः पद्मरागमणिविद्रुमभङ्गैः इन्द्रगोपनिकरैः स्थगिता भूः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पीतपुष्करकलापपयोभ्यः जलदेभ्यः निर्गतैः जलैः इव पद्मरागमणिविद्रुमभङ्गैः इन्द्रगोपनिकरैः भूः स्थगिता
commentaries.gemini_summary: The earth was covered with swarms of bright-red Indragopa insects resembling fragments of rubies and corals, appearing like raindrops shed by clouds that had drunk the reddish waters of lotus blossoms.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The Ganges flows in Nandanavana (the garden frequented by devathas) of Devendra, the enemy of the demon Paka. While flowing the tides of that river uprooted the trees there and carried their roots along with gold creeper that had spread on those trees. The lightning in the sky shone like that gold creeper falling down along with the roots of those trees which hitherto were protecting it.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: इन्द्रनील-कुल-नील-घन-आली-मध्य-वृत्ति-चपला इव चकाशे प्रावृट्-अब्जनयना चिकुराली यत्-अलक-उल्लसित-कुङ्कुम-रेखा
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: प्रावृट्-अब्जनयना चिकुराली यत्-अलक-उल्लसित-कुङ्कुम-रेखा इन्द्रनील-कुल-नील-घन-आली-मध्य-वृत्ति-चपला इव चकाशे।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The streak of saffron shining along the dark locks of the lotus-eyed maiden of the rainy season gleamed brilliantly, resembling a flash of lightning positioned in the midst of dark clouds that are as blue as sapphire gems.

44.sa: कुम्भसम्भवगुरोरुपदेशं प्राप्तकाम इव दक्षिणदेशम् । जृम्भमाणजलधौ जलपाने वारिवाहनिचयो विशति स्म ॥ ४४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Dense clouds would be hovering around in the sky during monsoon. Therefore it would be difficult to see the sun or the moon rising. The poet has dexterously described that one could know whether it is the sun or the moon that is rising by seeing the state of the lotus and the lily nearby. If the lotus has blossomed and the lily has remained as bud, it is the rising of the sun. On the other hand if the lily has blossomed and the lotus has remained as bud, it is the rising of the moon.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: कुम्भसम्भव-गुरोः उपदेशम् प्राप्तकामः इव दक्षिण-देशम् जृम्भमाण-जलधौ जल-पाने वारिवाह-निचयः विशति स्म
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: वारिवाहनिचयः कुम्भसम्भवगुरोः उपदेशं प्राप्तकामः इव जृम्भमाणजलधौ जलपाने दक्षिणदेशं विशति स्म ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: As if having received instructions from Sage Agastya (who famously drank the ocean) to accomplish its desire, the mass of clouds moved into the southern direction to drink water from the vast, surging ocean.

45.sa: पाकवैरिवनसिन्धुतरङ्गा कृष्टरूढतरुमूलकलापा । व्योम्नि विद्युदिव काञ्चनवल्ली काममभ्रभरिता निपतन्ती ॥ ४५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The poet has compared the days of summer (covered with clouds) to the elephants and the sun to a lion. He has described that when the sun ripped open those clouds (when the lion ripped open the kumbhas, the frontal globe on the upper part of the elephant's forehead) the monsoon set in. Then white hailstones accompanied by red fire flies fell on the earth. They appeared like pearls soaked in blood oozing out of pieces of flesh of the kumbhas of those elephants.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पाकवैरि-वन-सिन्धु-तरङ्ग-आकृष्ट-रूढ-तरु-मूल-कलापा व्योम्नि विद्युत् इव काञ्चन-वल्ली कामम् अभ्र-भरिता निपतन्ती
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पाकवैरि-वन-सिन्धु-तरङ्ग-आकृष्ट-रूढ-तरु-मूल-कलापा अभ्र-भरिता व्योम्नि निपतन्ती विद्युत् काञ्चन-वल्ली इव कामम् (अभात्)
commentaries.gemini_summary: Descending through the sky heavily laden with dark monsoon clouds and uprooting firmly grown trees by the forceful surge of the celestial river of Indra, the flash of lightning appeared intensely like a golden creeper.

46.sa: व्योम्नि सान्द्रतवारिदवृन्दे विद्युतासु विततासु समन्तात् । पुष्पवत्समुदयावनुमेयो फुल्लमीलितपयोरुहपङ्क्त्या ॥ ४६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The sun and the moon are the eyes of the Lord. When the Lord lies down on the body of Sesha in the ocean of milk during monsoon (When the Lord sleeps contemplantively during chathurmasya, the period of four months which the sanyasis spend is seclusion) he closes his eyes. Then the light from the sun and the moon become pale as they disappear from those eyes of the Lord. Thus the poet has interestingly described that the act of the Lord closing his eyes results in the resplendence of sun and moon turning pale.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: व्योम्नि सान्द्रत-वारिद-वृन्दे विद्युतासु विततासु समन्तात् पुष्पवत्-समुदयौ अनुमेयौ फुल्ल-मीलित-पयोरुह-पङ्क्त्या
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: व्योम्नि समन्तात् सान्द्रतवारिदवृन्दे विद्युतासु विततासु (सतीषु), फुल्लमीलितपयोरुहपङ्क्त्या पुष्पवत्समुदयौ अनुमेयौ (आस्ताम्) ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: When dense rainclouds and lightning spread across the entire sky concealing the luminaries, the presence of the sun and the moon could only be inferred indirectly through the blooming and closing of the rows of day- and night-lotuses.

47.sa: निर्गतानि दिवि सूर्यविभिन्नग्रीष्मवासरमदावलकुम्भात् । मौक्तिकानि सह मस्तकमांसैः सेन्द्रगोपकरका अनुचक्रुः ॥ ४७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The sun, master of the day was in a hapless state at the end of Dakshinayana as he had lost most of his rays and radiance. As a result of this, the days became shorter like loyal servants getting distressfully emaciated when their master loses his wealth. But those days became longer during Uttarayana as a result of monsoon setting in and the sun regaining his radiance.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: निर्गतानि दिवि सूर्य-विभिन्न-ग्रीष्म-वासर-मदावल-कुम्भात् मौक्तिकानि सह मस्तक-मांसैः स-इन्द्रगोप-करकाः अनुचक्रुः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सेन्द्रगोपकरकाः दिवि सूर्यविभिन्नग्रीष्मवासरमदावलकुम्भात् मस्तकमांसैः सह निर्गतानि मौक्तिकानि अनुचक्रुः ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The hailstones falling along with bright red indragopa insects resembled white pearls mixed with brain-flesh spilling into the sky from the temple of the summer-day elephant, which had been split open by the fierce sun.

48.sa: दुग्धवारिधिपयस्यधिवर्षं शार्ङ्गिणि स्वपति शेषशरीरे । मीलनान्नयनयोस्तनुलक्ष्म्यौ मेघपूर्णगगने द्युमनीन्दू ॥ ४८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Hemantha and Sishira Ruthus are the seasons of winter. As a result of nights getting longer because of the presence of clouds and non availability of sunlight for longer periods, the season turns non-conducive for copious growth of lotus, the sun's most favourite flower and they get withered. Those nights which grew longer by the grace of sun returned their favour by being helpful in the growth of those lotus flowers in plenty.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: दुग्धवारिधिपयसि अधिवर्षम् शार्ङ्गिणि स्वपति शेषशरीरे मीलनात् नयनयोः तनुलक्ष्म्यौ मेघपूर्णगगने द्युमणीन्दू
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अधिवर्षम् दुग्धवारिधिपयसि शेषशरीरे शार्ङ्गिणि स्वपति (सति) नयनयोः मीलनात् मेघपूर्णगगने द्युमणीन्दू तनुलक्ष्म्यौ (अभूताम्) ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: During the rainy season, when Lord Vishnu slumbers upon the serpent Shesha in the ocean of milk with His eyes closed, the sun and moon (representing His two eyes) lose their brilliance in the cloud-filled sky.

49.sa: स्वामिनिक्षतवसौ दिननाथे यत्पुराजनि दिनेष्वतिकार्श्यम् । तद्विमर्शमधिगम्य दिनानामद्य हृद्यत वासरवृद्धिः ॥ ४९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When the sun was shining brilliantly in the sky on full moon day in the month of Ashadha, Sri Raghavendra after worshipping Lord Sri Narayana whose eyes resembled the lotus, performed the sankalp of commencement of his vow of Chathurmasya accompanied by other great saints.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: स्वामिनि क्षतवसौ दिननाथे यत् पुरा अजनि दिनेषु अतिकार्श्यम् । तत् विमर्शम् अधिगम्य दिनानाम् अद्य हृद्यत वासरवृद्धिः ॥
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: स्वामिनि दिननाथे क्षतवसौ पुरा दिनेषु यत् अतिकार्श्यम् अजनि, दिनानाम् तत् विमर्शम् अधिगम्य अद्य वासरवृद्धिः हृद्यत ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The verse poetically reflects on the lengthening of days, stating that after considering the severe shortness the days had previously endured when their lord, the sun, was depleted of radiance, the increase in daytime has now become truly delightful.

50.sa: स्वप्रियां जलजनीं परिभूय प्रोर्मयत्तुहिनहन्तृदिनेभ्यः । तादृशी दिनकरे दिनवृद्धीर्या निशाक्षयविधावपि दक्षा ॥ ५० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The moon filled with all the sixteen moral stains shines brilliantly on full moonday in the month of Ashadha. When the sun was in the middle of the sky (at noon) on that day, the great saint Sri Raghavendra initiated the rites in respect of Chathurmasya with sankalpa after offering worship to Lord Sri Hari.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: स्वप्रियाम् जलजनीम् परिभूय प्रोर्मयत् तुहिनहन्तृ-दिनेभ्यः तादृशी दिनकरे दिनवृद्धिः या निशा-क्षय-विधौ अपि दक्षा
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: दिनकरे या दिनवृद्धिः स्वप्रियाम् जलजनीम् परिभूय तुहिनहन्तृ-दिनेभ्यः प्रोर्मयत्, तादृशी (सा) निशा-क्षय-विधौ अपि दक्षा (आसीत्)।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Under the radiant sun, the elongation of the daylight hours expanded beyond the standard solar days, proving equally efficient at steadily diminishing the duration of the nights.

51.sa: पूर्णिमाहनि सपूषणि मध्ये पुष्करं लसति पुष्करनेत्रम् । पूजयन् यतिवरैरिह चातुर्मास्यनामनियमं विदधाति ॥ ५१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra used to please Lord Sri Hari by offering special poojas and delivering discourses, etc. during Chathurmasya. The poet has exclaimed that if a virtous Brahmin could describe the grandeur of even a day's worship offered by Sri Raghavendra to the Lord during Chaturmasya, he could be termed as a great Vedic Scholar. Such a Brahmin is sure to attain renunciation expounded by the Vedas. Oh what a great fortune!! How could I describe the greatness of Sri Raghavendra!!!
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पूर्णिमा-अहनि सपूषणि मध्ये पुष्करम् लसति पुष्कर-नेत्रम् पूजयन् यति-वरैः इह चातुर्मास्य-नाम-नियमम् विदधाति
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पूर्णिमा-अहनि सपूषणि पुष्करम् मध्ये लसति (सति) पुष्कर-नेत्रम् पूजयन् यति-वरैः (सह) इह चातुर्मास्य-नाम-नियमम् विदधाति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: On the full moon day at midday, when the sun shines brightly in the center of the sky, Sri Raghavendra observes the sacred vow of Chaturmasya together with eminent ascetics while worshiping the lotus-eyed Lord.

52.sa: दुर्दिने हरिकटाक्षविहीने पङ्किले च समये समतीते । संप्रबुद्धहरिवीक्षणगोभूद्भासरोथ विशदीभवदाशः ॥ ५२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: As the whole sky was covered by the clouds, the sun was not visible. There was slush everywhere on the earth. These were the features of monsoon. Lord Sri Narayana who was sleeping for four months during Chaturmasya woke up at the end of the monsoon. As soon as the Lord set his eyes on those clouds, they completely disappeared and the sky became clearly visible. Thus Sharad Ruthu (Autumn) set in after the monsoon ended.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: दुर्दिने हरि-कटाक्ष-विहीने पङ्किले च समये समतीते संप्रबुद्ध-हरि-वीक्षण-गः अभूत् भासरः अथ विशदीभवत्-आशः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अथ दुर्दिने हरि-कटाक्ष-विहीने पङ्किले च समये समतीते संप्रबुद्ध-हरि-वीक्षण-गः विशदीभवत्-आशः भासरः अभूत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: When the dark, slushy monsoon season lacking Lord Hari's glance passed away, the awakened Lord opened His eyes; entering His line of sight, the bright sun (and the autumn season) arose, making all the directions clear and bright.

53.sa: मल्लिकाक्षनिवहेषु मनोज्ञेष्वम्बुजेषु मन्दिरेषु शरेषु । तत्रतत्र विशदं महिमानं दर्शयन् विहरति स्म स कालः ॥ ५३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Purity and whiteness were prominently visible everywhere during autumn. Even the Mallikaksha (A species of swan) birds and their filthy beaks and legs appeared immaculately clean. Beautiful white lotus looked still more whitish. The cloud appeared extremely whitish. The stem of kash straw with white flowers looked splendid. Thus the whole world appeared very beautiful as a result of whiteness spreading everywhere during the autumn.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मल्लिकाक्ष-निवहेषु मनोज्ञेषु अम्बुजेषु मन्दिरेषु शरेषु तत्र तत्र विशदं महिमानं दर्शयन् विहरति स्म सः कालः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सः कालः मल्लिकाक्षनिवहेषु मनोज्ञेषु अम्बुजेषु मन्दिरेषु शरेषु तत्र तत्र विशदं महिमानं दर्शयन् विहरति स्म।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Displaying its pure, white brilliance everywhere—among the flocks of wild geese, charming lotuses, mansions, and blossoming reeds—that autumn season revelled gracefully.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Lakshmi known as autumn was made to conceive by the fame of those kings who set out on their conquest. The flock of parrots visibly flying in the sky was like the rows of hair of Sharallakshmi. Whiteness appeared in her lovely bosoms.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: दिग्जय-उन्मुख-नृप-व्रज-कीर्त्या गर्भिणी-कृत-शरत्-दिन-लक्ष्म्याः व्यक्त-कीर-तति-रोम-लतायाः पाण्डिमा अजनि पयोधर-दृश्यः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: दिग्जय-उन्मुख-नृप-व्रज-कीर्त्या गर्भिणी-कृत-शरत्-दिन-लक्ष्म्याः व्यक्त-कीर-तति-रोम-लतायाः पयोधर-दृश्यः पाण्डिमा अजनि ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Impregnated, as it were, by the white fame of kings setting out on conquests, the goddess of Autumn—whose bodily line of hair was the visible flock of green parrots—developed a paleness seen upon her clouds (or breasts).

55.sa: वीक्ष्य संयमिवरस्य पयोदा दानकेलिमतुलां धनलक्ष्याः । हन्त वर्षविमुखाः समभूवन् पाण्डुरा भृशकृशाश्च शुचैव ॥ ५५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra was magnanimous in bestowing wealth on those who were devoted to him. When the clouds saw his magnanimity, they stopped showering rains, turned pale by being slighted and got emaciated from great worry. The clouds would not shower rains in the autumn. They look white and appear very thin as a result of deficiency of moisture. It appeared as if they stopped showering rains as they felt that the rains they shower were meagre when compared to the wealth showered by Sri Raghavendra. They also turned pale by being slighted and got emaciated from worry.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वीक्ष्य संयमिवरस्य पयोदाः दानकेलिम् अतुलाम् धनलक्ष्याः हन्त वर्षविमुखाः समभूवन् पाण्डुराः भृशकृशाः च शुचा एव
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पयोदाः संयमिवरस्य अतुलां धनलक्ष्याः दानकेलिं वीक्ष्य हन्त शुचा एव वर्षविमुखाः पाण्डुराः भृशकृशाः च समभूवन् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Upon witnessing the supreme ascetic's incomparable generosity in bestowing wealth, the clouds, as if out of sheer grief and humiliation, ceased raining and became pale and emaciated.

56.sa: आत्मनोभिमुखमागतमेनं वीक्ष्य संयमिवरं धनदाशाम् । हर्षितो नु विचचार तदग्रे हंसपालिरिव वारिदपुञ्जः ॥ ५६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The clouds which were as immaculate as a swan were delighted when they saw Sri Raghavendra coming in their direction. Then they, like paramahamsas (asceties of the highest order) follow their guru, began to follow the great saint who was moving towards north. Explanation: Sri Raghavendra was travelling towards north. The clouds would be naturally moving towards north in the autumn. It is the imagination of the poet that the clouds too were moving towards north following the great saint.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: आत्मनः अभिमुखम् आगतम् एनम् वीक्ष्य संयमिवरम् धनदाशाम् हर्षितः नु विचचार तदग्रे हंसपालिः इव वारिदपुञ्जः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: धनदाशाम् आत्मनः अभिमुखम् आगतम् एनम् संयमिवरम् वीक्ष्य हर्षितः वारिदपुञ्जः हंसपालिः इव तदग्रे विचचार नु ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Seeing the eminent ascetic approaching northwards towards its own direction, the flock of white clouds, as if overjoyed and resembling a row of swans, moved ahead before him.

57.sa: वारिदागमयुगान्तविरामे नैकरूपसरसीमिषशौरेः । नाभिपद्मनिवहा इव पद्मा व्यञ्जयन्त्यलिविधिं विलसन्तः ॥ ५७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: As autumn set in after the monsoon, bees started hovering around those lotus flowers abundantly grown in boundless number of lakes, just like Chathurmukha Brahma manifesting in the lotus emanating from the navel of Lord Sri Narayana. Explanation: The poet has figuratively compared the boundless number of lakes to Lord Sri Narayana, the lotus flowers grown in those lakes to the lotus emanating from his navel and the bees to Chathurmukha Brahma manifested in that flower.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वारिदागम-युगान्त-विरामे नैक-रूप-सरसी-मिष-शौरेः नाभिपद्म-निवहाः इव पद्माः व्यञ्जयन्ति अलि-विधिम् विलसन्तः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: वारिदागम-युगान्त-विरामे विलसन्तः पद्माः नैक-रूप-सरसी-मिष-शौरेः नाभिपद्म-निवहाः इव अलि-विधिम् व्यञ्जयन्ति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: At the end of the monsoon season, the blossoming lotuses in numerous lakes resembled the lotuses emerging from Lord Vishnu's navel, revealing the presence of bees just as the navel-lotus reveals the creator Brahma.

58.sa: उत्थितस्य सरसीरुहनाभेश्चन्द्रसूर्यनयनस्य तदानीम् । शंसतः स्म नलिनीरजनीशौ संप्रबोधमधिकं विलसन्तौ ॥ ५८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Lord Sri Narayana who has the lotus as his navel, the sun and the moon as his eyes woke up from his contemplatation sleep after Chaturmasya. The sun and the moon who were shining brilliantly during the autumn proclaimed that the Lord has woken up.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: उत्थितस्य सरसीरुहनाभेः चन्द्रसूर्यनयनस्य तदानीम् शंसतः स्म नलिनीरजनीशौ संप्रबोधम् अधिकम् विलसन्तौ
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तदानीम् अधिकम् विलसन्तौ नलिनीरजनीशौ उत्थितस्य चन्द्रसूर्यनयनस्य सरसीरुहनाभेः संप्रबोधम् शंसतः स्म ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: At that time, the sun and the moon, shining brilliantly, proclaimed the awakening of Lord Vishnu (the lotus-navelled one), whose very eyes are the sun and the moon.

59.sa: प्रावृडागमयुगान्तसमुद्यद्वारिवाहजलधौ विनिवृत्ते । सौकतोत्कर इव क्षणदायाश्चन्द्रिका बुधजनैरुदलेखि ॥ ५९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When those clouds (the sea) which prospered during the monsoon (destruction of the world) vanished (dried up) all the wise men exaggerated that the moon light in the autumn looked like sand.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: प्रावृट्-आगम-युगान्त-समुद्यत्-वारिवाह-जलधौ विनिवृत्ते सैकतोत्करः इव क्षणदायाः चन्द्रिका बुधजनैः उदलेखि
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: प्रावृडागमयुगान्तसमुद्यद्वारिवाहजलधौ विनिवृत्ते क्षणदायाः चन्द्रिका बुधजनैः सैकतोत्करः इव उदलेखि ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: When the ocean of clouds that rose during the monsoon (like the deluge at the end of an era) receded, wise poets described the moonlight of the night as if it were a vast expanse of glistening sand left behind on the shore.

60.sa: काम्यकर्मचयभञ्जनहेतूभूतदर्शनमिमं यमिधुर्यम् । वीक्ष्य बिभ्यदिव तत्फलभूतं शालिवृन्दमभवद्व्यनम्रम् ॥ ६० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra has great knowledge of the truth that Lord Sri Hari destroys any act done with the purpose of getting the wish fulfilled. When the paddy trees which were bearing the fruits of cultivation, an act done with the aim, in the form of spikes of paddy on their tops saw the saint of such greatness, they stooped down as if they were frightened.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: काम्यकर्मचयभञ्जनहेतूभूतदर्शनम् इमम् यमिधुर्यम् वीक्ष्य बिभ्यत् इव तत्फलभूतम् शालिवृन्दम् अभवत् व्यनम्रम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: काम्यकर्मचयभञ्जनहेतूभूतदर्शनम् इमम् यमिधुर्यम् वीक्ष्य तत्फलभूतम् शालिवृन्दम् बिभ्यत् इव व्यनम्रम् अभवत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Upon seeing the eminent ascetic (Raghavendra), whose mere sight destroys the accumulation of desire-prompted actions, the cluster of paddy plants (the fruit of such desired effort) bent low as if frightened.

61.sa: प्रावृडाहितजलाक्रमभङ्गां सस्यमञ्जरिविभूषितगात्रीम् । मातरं क्षितिमवेक्ष्य वनाली पक्वदाडिम फलेन जहास ॥ ६१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Heavy showers during the monsoon had created cliffs and pits all over the earth. Mounds of soil could be seen everywhere. Spikes of corn had decorated the entire body of Bhoodevi. The range of forests which saw Bhoodevi laughed through its mouth which was in the form of ripe and riven pomegranate fruits. Explanation: Cliffs and pits caused by the force of showers during the monsoon could be seen all over the ground, during the autumn. Spikes grew in the plants of paddy and other grains. Ripe and riven pomegranate fruits in abundance could be seen everywhere in the forests. These were the features of the autumn.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: प्रावृडाहितजलाक्रमभङ्गाम् सस्यमञ्जरिविभूषितगात्रीम् मातरम् क्षितिम् अवेक्ष्य वनाली पक्वदाडिमफलेन जहास
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: वनाली प्रावृडाहितजलाक्रमभङ्गाम् सस्यमञ्जरिविभूषितगात्रीम् मातरम् क्षितिम् अवेक्ष्य पक्वदाडिमफलेन जहास ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Beholding Mother Earth decorated with fresh grain sprouts after the torrential downpours of the monsoon, the range of forests seemed to smile with delight through its split, ripe pomegranate fruits.

62.sa: मातुलङ्गलतिकामिह चूते स्प्रष्टुमुद्यतिफलस्तनमभ्ये । मोहिते च मरुता वनराजिः पक्वदाडिमफलेन जहास ॥ ६२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: When the cool and fragrant wind blew during the autumn, the mango tree fainted as a result of intoxication of impassionate love. When it swung sideways and touched the citron tree that stood nearby, it appeared as if it was trying to get the feel of the citron fruit that had grown on the branch of the citron tree and resembled the attractive bosoms of a beautiful girl. Seeing the impassionate act of love of the young mango tree, the range of forests looked like laughting through its mouth which was in the form of ripe and riven pomegranate fruits.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मातुलङ्ग-लतिकाम् इह चूते स्प्रष्टुम् उद्यति फल-स्तनम् अभ्ये मोहिते च मरुता वनराजिः पक्व-दाडिम-फलेन जहास
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: इह मरुता मोहिते चूते अभ्ये फल-स्तनं मातुलङ्ग-लतिकां स्प्रष्टुम् उद्यति (सति) च वनराजिः पक्व-दाडिम-फलेन जहास ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: When the mango tree, intoxicated by the gentle breeze, swayed eagerly to touch the nearby citron-creeper whose fruits resembled breasts, the forest row appeared to burst into laughter at this romantic overture through its split-open, ripe pomegranates.

63.sa: भानुमालिनि गतेथ तुलायां रामनाथपुरमेत्य चिराय । सह्यभूधरसुतासलिलेस्मिन्मज्जनेन मुदितोभवदेषः ॥ ६३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Hemantha Ruthu which was like ash and such other powders that infatuated the girls who were disunited with their sweethearts; which was like the dust raised by the soldiers of a king that destroyed the lotus; which was decorated with small drizzles of glaciers resembling the bunches of pearls adorning the small mantap in the sky, set in.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: भानुमालिनि गते अथ तुलायां रामनाथपुरम् एत्य चिराय सह्यभूधरसुतासलिले अस्मिन् मज्जनेन मुदितः अभवत् एषः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अथ भानुमालिनि तुलायां गते एषः रामनाथपुरम् एत्य चिराय अस्मिन् सह्यभूधरसुतासलिले मज्जनेन मुदितः अभवत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: When the sun entered the zodiac sign of Libra (Tulā), he arrived at Ramanathapuram and was filled with joy after taking a holy bath for a long duration in the waters of the Kaveri (the daughter of the Sahya mountain).

64.sa: मानिनीजनविमोहनचूर्णैः सारसेषु नृपसैन्यरजोभिः । व्योममण्डपकमौक्तिकगुच्छैराविरास समयो हिमपूरैः ॥ ६४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: In Hemantha Ruthu, the sun who could not see Padmini, (the lotus garden) lost his resplendence as he was covered by dense fog. Padmini too appeared to be covered by maze as she was struck with grief for not being able to see the sun.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मानिनीजनविमोहनचूर्णैः सारसेषुनृपसैन्यरजोभिः व्योममण्डपकमौक्तिकगुच्छैः आविरास समयः हिमपूरैः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मानिनीजनविमोहनचूर्णैः सारसेषुनृपसैन्यरजोभिः व्योममण्डपकमौक्तिकगुच्छैः हिमपूरैः समयः आविरास
commentaries.gemini_summary: The winter season arrived laden with abundant snow and mist, which appeared like an enchanting powder to charm proud women, the dust raised by the advancing army of King Cupid, and clusters of pearls hanging from the celestial canopy.

65.sa: पद्मिनीमनवलोक्य पतङ्गो मन्ददीधितिरिहास हिमौघैः । रव्यादर्शनवशादिव शोकादब्जिनी च तुहिनैः किमु लीना ॥ ६५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: As the Shishira Ruthu set in, the sun who was afraid of the winter, intended to move towards south east. Vayu, his attendant appeared to have already gone there to confirm the presence of Agni there. Explanation: Vayu is the attendant of both Agni and the sun, the embodiment of resplendence. It appeared as though Vayu had already moved towards south east to facilitate Agni dazzle so that his master, the sun could get himself warmed just like the servants go to the place in advance and prepare for the stay of their king there. When Shishira Ruthu sets in, the sun moves towards south east and the chilly wind blows from that direction.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पद्मिनीम् अनवलोक्य पतङ्गः मन्ददीधितिः इह आस हिमौघैः । रवि-अदर्शन-वशात् इव शोकात् अब्जिनी च तुहिनैः किमु लीना ॥
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पतङ्गः पद्मिनीम् अनवलोक्य हिमौघैः इह मन्ददीधितिः आस । अब्जिनी च रवि-अदर्शन-वशात् शोकात् इव तुहिनैः लीना किमु ॥
commentaries.gemini_summary: In the cold season, unable to behold the lotus cluster, the sun became dim among masses of frost; in turn, as if out of grief at not seeing the sun, the lotus cluster disappeared under the snow.

66.sa: उष्णारश्मिरधिकं हिमभीतो हव्यवाहदिशमिच्छति गन्तुम् । अग्निरस्त्युत न वेति विवेक्तुं प्रागयादिव समीरणचारः ॥ ६६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: After having the darshan of Lord Sri Vittala at Pandharapura, the great saint Sri Raghavendra reached Kolhapura. He stayed there for many days worshipping Lord Sri Moolarama.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: उष्णारश्मिः अधिकम् हिमभीतः हव्यवाहदिशम् इच्छति गन्तुम् अग्निः अस्ति उत न वा इति विवेक्तुम् प्राक् अयात् इव समीरणचारः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: हिमभीतः उष्णारश्मिः अधिकम् हव्यवाहदिशम् गन्तुम् इच्छति (तत्र) अग्निः अस्ति उत न वा इति विवेक्तुम् प्राक् समीरणचारः अयात् इव ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Extremely afraid of the winter cold, the sun wished to head towards the direction of the fire-god (the South). It seemed as though the wind proceeded in advance as a spy to ascertain whether fire actually existed there or not.

67.sa: पाण्डुरङ्गपुरविठ्ठलमीक्ष्य प्रस्थितः स करवीरपुराख्यम् । पत्तनं विरचयन्हरिपूजां तत्र वासमकरोच्चिरकालम् ॥ ६७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Leaving from there, Sri Raghavendra reached Ramanathapura. Then at the time of the sun entering Thula rasi, he rejoiced by taking holy bath plunging into the river Cauvery which was renowned as the destroyer of sins.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पाण्डुरङ्गपुरविठ्ठलम् ईक्ष्य प्रस्थितः सः करवीरपुराख्यम् पत्तनम् विरचयन् हरिपूजाम् तत्र वासम् अकरोत् चिरकालम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पाण्डुरङ्गपुरविठ्ठलम् ईक्ष्य प्रस्थितः सः करवीरपुराख्यम् पत्तनम् विरचयन् हरिपूजाम् तत्र चिरकालम् वासम् अकरोत्
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having had darshana of Lord Vitthala at Pandharpur, he departed and reached the city called Karavirapura (Kolhapur), where he resided for a long time while devotedly conducting the worship of Lord Hari.

68.sa: गौतमाघपरिहारिणि तोये स्नानकर्म विरचय्य स विद्वान् । पूजितः प्रतिपदं प्रथितधीभिः प्राविशत्किल पुरीं विजयाख्याम् ॥ ६८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Then Sri Raghavendra, the learned saint took holy bath in Godavari, the river that destroyed the sins of saint Gouthama. Proceeding from there and receiving felicitations from his antagonists everywhere on his way, he entered the town of Vijaya, on the banks of the river Godavari.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: गौतमाघपरिहारिणि तोये स्नानकर्म विरचय्य सः विद्वान् पूजितः प्रतिपदम् प्रथितधीभिः प्राविशत् किल पुरीम् विजयाख्याम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सः विद्वान् गौतमाघपरिहारिणि तोये स्नानकर्म विरचय्य प्रथितधीभिः प्रतिपदम् पूजितः विजयाख्याम् पुरीम् प्राविशत् किल ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having performed his ritual bath in the purifying waters of the Godavari River (which absolved Sage Gautama of sin), the learned saint Raghavendra, honored at every step by renowned scholars, entered the town called Vijaya.

69.sa: मुद्रयारिदरयोर्मिलितान्योरङ्कितानकृत शिष्यसमूहान् । वादिनोपि परिभूय विशिष्य श्वेतमातपनिवारणमाप ॥ ६९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra, the king of saints sanctified his disciples by Tapta mudradharana with hot seals of chakra (wheel) and shankha (conch). When the scholars of the royal court of Vijayanagara engaged him in debate, he defeated all those scholars and received felicitations from the king with honour of shwetha chatra (White umbrella) as a sign of victory.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मुद्रया अरिदरयोः मिलितान् यः अङ्कितान् अकृत शिष्यसमूहान् वादिनः अपि परिभूय विशिष्य श्वेतम् आतपनिवारणम् आप
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यः मिलितान् शिष्यसमूहान् अरिदरयोः मुद्रया अङ्कितान् अकृत वादिनः अपि विशिष्य परिभूय श्वेतम् आतपनिवारणम् आप ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: He sanctified the assembled groups of disciples by stamping them with the sacred seals of the discus and conch, and after thoroughly refuting rival scholars in debate, he was honoured with a royal white umbrella.

70.sa: स्नातवानथ बुधैः सह कृष्णानिम्नगापयसि निर्जितमारः । तत्तटे जयगुरूक्तटीकां व्याकृतापि यतिराडणुभाष्यं ॥ ७० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra who had a very beautiful visual personality left Vijayanagar accompanied by many scholars and reached the banks of the river Krishna where he took a holy dip. Then he stayed there for many days and wrote "Bhavadeepa" as a gloss on "Tatvaprakashika" a commentary of Sri Jayatheertha on "Brahma soothra Bhashya" of Sri Madhwacharya. He also wrote "Tatvamanjari" as commentary on Anubhashya of Sri Acharya.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: स्नातवान् अथ बुधैः सह कृष्णानिम्नगा-पयसि निर्जित-मारः तत्तटे जयगुरु-उक्त-टीकाम् व्याकृत अपि यति-राट् अणु-भाष्यम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अथ निर्जितमारः यतिराट् बुधैः सह कृष्णानिम्नगापयसि स्नातवान् तत्तटे जयगुरूक्तटीकाम् अणुभाष्यम् अपि व्याकृत
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having conquered desire (or possessing beauty surpassing Cupid), the great ascetic Raghavendra bathed in the waters of the river Krishna along with learned scholars, and on its bank, composed commentaries on the gloss of Sri Jayatirtha as well as on the Anubhashya.

71.sa: तत्रतत्र विरचय्य स वासं पुण्यभूषु पुरुषोत्तमभक्तः । श्रीमहीधरमुपेत्य च तुङ्गं वेङ्कटेशमवलोकितुमागात् ॥ ७१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: After staying at many holy places on his pilgrimage, Sri Raghavendra who occupied the first place among the men of profound devotion in Lord Sri Hari reached Srishyla where he had the darshan of Shrishyla Mallikarjuna. Then he left for the holy town of Tirupati to have the darshan of Sri Srinivasa, the supreme Lord.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: तत्र तत्र विरचय्य सः वासम् पुण्यभूषु पुरुषोत्तम-भक्तः श्री-महीधरम् उपेत्य च तुङ्गम् वेङ्कटेशम् अवलोकितुम् आगात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पुरुषोत्तमभक्तः सः तत्र तत्र पुण्यभूषु वासं विरचय्य तुङ्गं श्रीमहीधरम् उपेत्य च वेङ्कटेशम् अवलोकितुम् आगात् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Staying at various sacred spots along the way, that supreme devotee of the Lord visited the lofty holy mountain (Srisailam) and then proceeded to Tirupati to behold Lord Venkatesha.

72.sa: नत्वा देवं वेङ्कटेशं यतीन्द्रः कृत्वा वासं वासरान्कांश्चिदत्र । काञ्चीमागात्काञ्चनागाररम्यां नत्वा विष्णुं चानमत्पार्वतीशम् ॥ ७२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra, the great saint who had the darshan of Lord Sri Venkateshwara at Thirumala paid his obeisance to the Lord with profound devotion and stayed there itself for some days. Then he reached Kancheepuram, a town splendidly shining with mansions of gold. After worshipping Lord Sri Hari known as Sri Varadaraja at Vishnukanchi he came to Shivakanchi and paid his obeisance to Sri Maharudra, the consort of Parvathidevi.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: नत्वा देवम् वेङ्कटेशम् यतीन्द्रः कृत्वा वासम् वासरान् कांश्चित् अत्र काञ्चीम् आगात् काञ्चन-आगार-रम्याम् नत्वा विष्णुम् च अनमत् पार्वती-ईशम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यतीन्द्रः देवम् वेङ्कटेशम् नत्वा अत्र कांश्चित् वासरान् वासम् कृत्वा काञ्चनागाररम्याम् काञ्चीम् आगात्, विष्णुम् नत्वा पार्वतीशम् च अनमत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: After bowing to Lord Venkatesha and staying there for some days, the eminent saint reached the city of Kanchi, adorned with golden mansions; there, after paying obeisance to Lord Vishnu, he also bowed to Lord Shiva.

73.sa: शोणाद्रिमासाद्य निषेव्य शम्भुं वृद्धाचलं प्राप्य विलोक्य रुद्रम् । श्रीमुष्णमभ्येत्य वराहरूपं विष्णुं प्रणम्यैष नुतिं व्यतानीत् ॥ ७३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Gurusarvabhouma worshipped Sri Parameshwara at Arunachala and came to Vriddha chala, a Shaivate place where he had the darshan of Sri Maharudra, its presiding deity. Proceeding from there he reached the holy town of Srimushna and worshipped Lord Sri Varaha, an incarnation of Lord Sri Mahavishnu, extolling the Lord in profound devotion.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: शोणाद्रिम् आसाद्य निषेव्य शम्भुम् वृद्धाचलम् प्राप्य विलोक्य रुद्रम् श्रीमुष्णम् अभ्येत्य वराह-रूपम् विष्णुम् प्रणम्य एषः नुतिम् व्यतानीत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: एषः शोणाद्रिम् आसाद्य शम्भुम् निषेव्य वृद्धाचलम् प्राप्य रुद्रम् विलोक्य श्रीमुष्णम् अभ्येत्य वराहरूपम् विष्णुम् प्रणम्य नुतिम् व्यतानीत्।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Having visited Sonadri (Arunachala) to worship Shambhu, and then Vriddhachala to behold Rudra, he proceeded to Srimushnam, where he bowed before Lord Vishnu in the form of Varaha and sang His praises.

74.sa: कृत्वा दिग्विजयमुपागतस्य दूरे कावेरीशिशिरजलावलोकमात्रात् । यत्सौख्यं समजनि तत्सुखं मुरारेः प्रायः स्यादिति यदि का कथेतरेषाम् ॥ ७४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra reached the banks of the river Cauvery after completing his journey to many far off places. Probably the extreme joy experienced by him by just beholding the splendor of the cool Cauvery must have been experienced by only Lord Sri Hari! Then how can I describe his experience of that happiness to others? Is it possible? The joy one experiences by beholding the beauty of Cauvery is extraordinary!!!!
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: कृत्वा दिग्विजयम् उपागतस्य दूरे कावेरी-शिशिर-जल-अवलोक-मात्रात् यत् सौख्यम् समजनि तत् सुखम् मुरारेः प्रायः स्यात् इति यदि का कथा इतरेषाम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: दिग्विजयम् कृत्वा उपागतस्य दूरे कावेरी-शिशिर-जल-अवलोक-मात्रात् यत् सौख्यम् समजनि, तत् सुखम् प्रायः मुरारेः स्यात् इति यदि, इतरेषाम् का कथा?
commentaries.gemini_summary: Upon returning after his victorious tour, the mere sight of the Kaveri's cool waters from afar brought him a bliss so immense that perhaps only Lord Murari could experience its like; what then can be said of ordinary beings?

75.sa: श्रीकुम्भघोणनगरीं प्रविशत्युदारां रामार्चयोरुतपसैव कृशे यतीन्द्रे । मन्ये कथं नु जनतामहितामयोध्यां रामेण तेन भरतेन कृतप्रवेशाम् ॥ ७५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra had gone down considerably by practicing religious vows constantly. After completing his journey, he entered the beautiful and populous town of Kumbhakonam carrying the idol of Lord Sri Moolarama along with him. When Sri Rama after killing Ravana came to Nandigrama, Bharatha who had gone down with grief of separation from Sri Rama by being constantly under penance entered the beautiful and the big town of Ayodhya along with Sri Rama. Then why can't I treat Kumbhakonam as Ayodhya when Sri Raghavendra, who was emacipated by constantly performing penance, entered it along with the idol of Lord Sri Moolarama?
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्री-कुम्भघोण-नगरीम् प्रविशति उदाराम् राम-अर्चया उरु-तपसा एव कृशे यति-इन्द्रे मन्ये कथम् नु जनता-महिताम् अयोध्याम् रामेण तेन भरतेन कृत-प्रवेशाम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: रामार्चया उरु-तपसा एव कृशे यतीन्द्रे उदाराम् श्री-कुम्भघोण-नगरीम् प्रविशति (सति), तेन रामेण भरतेन कृत-प्रवेशाम् जनता-महिताम् अयोध्याम् कथम् नु मन्ये?
commentaries.gemini_summary: As the supreme ascetic, emaciated by intense penance and devotion to the idol of Rama, entered the grand city of Kumbhakonam, the poet ponders how anyone could not view this city as Ayodhya itself, celebrated by the people, being entered by Bharata alongside Sri Rama.

76.sa: प्रहृष्टेन चित्तेन मध्येप्रतोल्यां महावीरविलासेन तात्कालिकेन । भुजङ्गप्रयातेन भूदेववन्द्यो हनुमन्तमित्थं प्रणौति स्म देवम् ॥ ७६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: While Sri Raghavendra was entering the town of Kumbhakonam, he was captivating with lustre and majesty manifested just then on his face. Many Brahmins were extolling and prostrating before him on his way. The scholarly Sri Raghavendra while walking on the main street saw the idol of Sri Hanumantha, his tutelary deity that was established by Sri Vyasaraja on the banks of the Hemapushkarni near the temple of Lord Sarangapani. Then extolling Sri Hanumantha with a self composed verse in Bhujagaprayata metre he prostrated before the idol.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: प्रहृष्टेन चित्तेन मध्येप्रतोल्याम् महावीर-विलासेन तात्कालिकेन भुजङ्गप्रयातेन भूदेव-वन्द्यः हनुमन्तम् इत्थम् प्रणौति स्म देवम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: भूदेव-वन्द्यः तात्कालिकेन महावीर-विलासेन प्रहृष्टेन चित्तेन मध्येप्रतोल्याम् भुजङ्ग-प्रयातेन देवम् हनुमन्तम् इत्थम् प्रणौति स्म ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Revered by the brahmins, Sri Raghavendra, filled with joy and radiating a momentary heroic majesty, extolled Lord Hanuman in the middle of the main street with hymns in the Bhujangaprayata metre.

77.sa: वाद्यैश्चित्रैः शङ्खभेरीमृदङ्गैः फुल्लैः पुष्पैर्विविधमनुजैः कीर्यमाणैः समन्तात् । वीथ्यावीथ्यां युवतिकरगारातर्तिके राघवेन्द्रो रामे पूर्वं प्रविशति मठं प्राविशत्संपदाढ्यम् ॥ ७७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: While the sounds of different musical instruments like trumpet, kettle drum, mridangam, conch, cymbols, veena, flute, etc. were getting reverberated from all directions; while people of different castes and creed were showering blossomed flowers all along the route; while young girls were performing Arathi in every street; Sri Raghavendra along with the idol of Lord Moolarama entered his Mutt that was shining opulently.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वाद्यैः चित्रैः शङ्ख-भेरी-मृदङ्गैः फुल्लैः पुष्पैः विविध-मनुजैः कीर्यमाणैः समन्तात् वीथ्यां-वीथ्याम् युवति-कर-ग-आरार्तिके राघवेन्द्रः रामे पूर्वम् प्रविशति मठम् प्राविशत् सम्पद्-आढ्यम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: चित्रैः शङ्खभेरीमृदङ्गैः वाद्यैः समन्तात् विविधमनुजैः कीर्यमाणैः फुल्लैः पुष्पैः वीथ्यां वीथ्याम् युवतिकरगारार्तिके रामे पूर्वम् प्रविशति राघवेन्द्रः सम्पदाढ्यम् मठम् प्राविशत्
commentaries.gemini_summary: Amidst the playing of diverse musical instruments such as conches, kettle-drums, and mridangas, the showering of blossoming flowers by all kinds of people, and the waving of arati lamps by young maidens along every street, Raghavendra entered the opulent mutt just after Lord Rama was brought inside.

78.sa: श्रीमत्कश्यपवंशवार्धिशशिनः षड्दर्शनीवल्लभ- श्रीलक्ष्मीनरसिंहवित्तविदुषः श्रीवेङ्कटाम्बामणौ । जातेनार्यदयासुधामयगिरा नारायणेनोदिते काव्ये चारुणि राघवेन्द्रविजये सर्गो जयत्यष्टमः ॥ ७८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Thus concludes the eighth canto of the epic "Sri Raghavendra Vijaya" enchanting with nectareous words composed by Narayanacharya with the blessings of his father. Narayanacharya who had his education from his father was the son of the couple Venkatamba and Lakshminarayanacharya who was an erudite scholar in all the six shastras and who was born and shone like a moon in the ocean of Kashyapagothra named after that virtuous and scholarly sage Kashyapa. English translation of the eighth canto of the epic "Sri Raghavendravijaya" composed by Sri Narayanacharya concluded.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रीमत्-कश्यप-वंश-वार्धि-शशिनः षड्दर्शनी-वल्लभ-श्री-लक्ष्मीनरसिंह-वित्त-विदुषः श्री-वेङ्कटाम्बा-मणौ जातेन आर्य-दया-सुधामय-गिरा नारायणेन उदिते काव्ये चारुणि राघवेन्द्रविजये सर्गः जयति अष्टमः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: श्रीमत्-कश्यप-वंश-वार्धि-शशिनः षड्दर्शनी-वल्लभ-श्री-लक्ष्मीनरसिंह-वित्त-विदुषः श्री-वेङ्कटाम्बा-मणौ जातेन आर्य-दया-सुधामय-गिरा नारायणेन उदिते चारुणि राघवेन्द्रविजये काव्ये अष्टमः सर्गः जयति।
commentaries.gemini_summary: This concluding colophon declares victory to the eighth canto of the delightful poem Raghavendra Vijaya, composed with nectarous words by Narayanacharya, who was born to Venkatamba and Lakshminarasimha—an eminent scholar of the six darshanas and the moon rising from the ocean of the Kashyapa lineage.
